stories.headline: Young India sports varsity to be ready by December 2028, says Chief Minister
stories.what: A Chief Minister has announced that the Young India sports university will be ready by December 2028, signalling a significant investment in elite sports infrastructure and athlete development in India. The announcement reflects a broader national push to build institutional frameworks for sports education and high-performance training that can produce future Olympic and international champions. The Times of India reported the Chief Minister's commitment to the December 2028 deadline, which is timed to align with the post-Los Angeles Olympics cycle.
stories.lens: A dedicated sports university could transform how India trains and produces elite athletes, giving young players from across the country structured pathways to professional sport at a time when India is pushing to raise its Olympic medal tally.
stories.article:
A new sports university under the 'Young India' banner is on track to become operational by December 2028, a Chief Minister announced, setting a firm deadline for what is intended to be a landmark institution for elite athlete development in the country. The Times of India reported the commitment, which marks a significant step in India's ambition to build world-class sports infrastructure.

The timing of the December 2028 deadline is notable — it falls shortly after the Los Angeles Olympic Games, positioning the institution as a cornerstone of India's longer-term sporting ambitions rather than a short-term fix. A dedicated sports varsity would provide structured academic and athletic training under one roof, a model that has proven successful in countries like the United States, Australia, and China.

India has long struggled to convert its enormous population into proportionate Olympic success, and successive governments have identified the lack of professional sports education infrastructure as a key gap. A full-fledged sports university, with dedicated coaching staff, sports science facilities, and academic programmes, would address that gap in a systematic way.

The announcement will be welcomed by athletes, coaches, and sports administrators who have long called for greater institutional investment. With India's cricket ecosystem already among the world's most developed, the challenge — and the opportunity — lies in building similar depth across Olympic disciplines. The Young India sports varsity, if delivered on time, could be a meaningful step in that direction.
key_facts: Young India sports university to be operational by December 2028
Chief Minister confirmed the deadline
Institution aimed at producing elite athletes and sports professionals

stories.headline: IFFM 2026 Nominations: Aamir Khan, Mammootty and Rishab Shetty Lead the Pack
stories.what: The Indian Film Festival of Melbourne (IFFM) 2026 nominations have been announced, with Aamir Khan, Mammootty and Rishab Shetty emerging as top contenders in the acting categories. The nominations span Hindi, Malayalam and Kannada cinema, reflecting the festival's pan-Indian scope. IFFM has grown into one of the most prestigious Indian film festivals held abroad, and the nominations signal which films and performances are being recognised on the international stage this year.
stories.lens: When Indian films and stars earn nominations at global festivals like IFFM, it boosts the international profile of regional cinema — a win not just for Bollywood but for Malayalam and Kannada films increasingly competing on the world stage.
stories.article:
The Indian Film Festival of Melbourne has unveiled its 2026 nominations, with three of Indian cinema's biggest names — Aamir Khan, Mammootty, and Rishab Shetty — among the top contenders for acting honours. The announcement underscores a broader trend: IFFM is no longer a Bollywood-exclusive affair, with Malayalam and Kannada cinema firmly in the conversation.

Mammootty and Rishab Shetty's presence in the nominations is particularly significant. Mammootty has been on an extraordinary late-career run, while Rishab Shetty rode the massive success of the Kantara franchise to become one of Indian cinema's most talked-about figures. Their nominations alongside Aamir Khan — known for his selective, high-stakes projects — makes this one of the most competitive IFFM fields in recent memory.

IFFM, held annually in Melbourne, Australia, has steadily grown in stature as a platform that celebrates Indian films for global audiences. It often serves as a bellwether for which performances and productions have resonated beyond domestic box-office metrics, lending the nominations a prestige beyond the awards circuit alone.

With the nominations now public, attention turns to the eventual winners and whether the ceremony will reinforce the momentum of pan-Indian cinema or see Bollywood reassert its dominance. For Indian film lovers both at home and in the Indian diaspora, the IFFM results are eagerly watched.
key_facts: Aamir Khan, Mammootty and Rishab Shetty are top contenders
Nominations span Hindi, Malayalam and Kannada cinema
IFFM 2026 nominations announced by NDTV

stories.headline: No Sairat 2: Director Nagraj Manjule Gives His Definitive Answer
stories.what: Director Nagraj Manjule has revealed his definitive plans regarding a sequel to Sairat, the landmark 2016 Marathi film that became one of Indian cinema's biggest crossover successes. Sairat's story of young love across caste lines struck a deep cultural chord and its tragic ending left audiences both devastated and hungry for more. Manjule's clarity on the sequel question settles years of speculation, though the nature of his answer — whether it is a firm no or a conditional possibility — remains the crux of the story.
stories.lens: Sairat wasn't just a hit film — it was a social phenomenon that brought caste discrimination into mainstream conversation; Manjule's decision on a sequel carries weight both as a creative and a cultural statement.
stories.article:
Nagraj Manjule, the director whose 2016 Marathi film Sairat shattered box-office records and redefined what regional Indian cinema could achieve, has finally addressed the question that has lingered for nearly a decade: will there be a Sairat 2?

Manjule revealed his definitive plans to The Indian Express, settling what has been one of the most persistent rumours in Marathi and broader Indian film circles. Sairat, which told the story of a romance across caste lines culminating in a shocking act of honour violence, was not only a massive commercial hit but a cultural watershed — it forced mainstream audiences and commentators to reckon with the brutal reality of caste-based social policing in rural Maharashtra.

The film launched the careers of its lead actors and inspired a Hindi remake, Dhadak, starring Janhvi Kapoor and Ishaan Khatter. Yet Manjule's original has retained a status that the remake could not replicate — its raw, earthy aesthetic and commitment to its characters' social reality gave it an authenticity that resonated far beyond Maharashtra.

Whether Manjule's answer is a clean no or a more nuanced position, the director's willingness to address it publicly suggests he is aware that Sairat belongs as much to its audience as to him. His definitive statement will allow both fans and the industry to finally move forward with clarity on one of Indian cinema's most discussed 'what ifs'.
key_facts: Director Nagraj Manjule has revealed his plans on a Sairat sequel
Sairat (2016) was a landmark Marathi crossover blockbuster
Film explored caste-based honour violence; inspired Hindi remake Dhadak

stories.headline: Saif Ali Khan: Bollywood 'Needs to Be Brave' After Rs 3,100 Crore Dhurandhar Hit
stories.what: Saif Ali Khan has called on Bollywood to be braver in its storytelling choices, drawing on the blockbuster success of Dhurandhar, which reportedly crossed Rs 3,100 crore at the box office. Speaking in the film's aftermath, Saif reflected on what the film's extraordinary performance signals for the industry — that bold, high-stakes content can find massive audiences. His comments come at a moment when the debate about Hindi cinema's creative direction versus commercial pressures is especially sharp.
stories.lens: A Rs 3,100 crore hit from a Bollywood production is a rare event — and when the star uses that platform to argue for creative risk-taking, it directly shapes what kind of films get greenlit next, affecting what Indian audiences will see in cinemas over the next few years.
stories.article:
Saif Ali Khan has used the extraordinary commercial success of Dhurandhar to make a pointed argument: Bollywood needs to be braver. The film, which crossed Rs 3,100 crore in box-office collections, has become one of the biggest talking points in the industry, and Saif's public reflection adds an intellectual dimension to its commercial triumph.

In his comments, Saif emphasised that the film's performance is not just a box-office milestone but a proof of concept — that Indian audiences are ready for ambitious, unconventional storytelling if the execution is right. The implicit critique is directed at a Bollywood culture that has often retreated to formulaic safety, particularly after a string of big-budget disappointments in recent years.

Dhurandhar's success is especially notable given the ongoing debate about the rise of south Indian films and their impact on Hindi cinema's market share. A blockbuster of this scale from a Bollywood production sends a signal that the industry can still compete when it commits fully to its vision.

Saif has also separately spoken about his film Kartavya, admitting that he felt the ending was flawed and that the villain should have faced greater consequences — a candour that has been widely noted. Taken together, his recent interviews paint the picture of a star willing to critically engage with the industry's challenges and his own work at a high-water moment in his recent career.
key_facts: Dhurandhar reportedly crossed Rs 3,100 crore at the box office
Saif Ali Khan calls for Bollywood to 'be brave'
Comments made in the context of the film's massive commercial success

stories.headline: Diljit Dosanjh Sidesteps US Citizenship Question With a Green Card Joke
stories.what: Singer-actor Diljit Dosanjh has deflected questions about whether he is seeking US citizenship, responding to the query with a joke about a Green Card and declining to confirm or deny anything. The exchange highlighted the curiosity surrounding his personal life as his global profile has grown enormously, fuelled by record-breaking international concert tours. For many Indian fans, Diljit occupies a rare position as both a pop culture phenomenon and an emblem of Punjabi identity, making questions about his national ties especially loaded.
stories.lens: Diljit Dosanjh is currently one of India's biggest global crossover stars — any hint that he may be relocating or changing citizenship touches a nerve among fans who see him as representing India and Punjab on the world stage.
stories.article:
Diljit Dosanjh, the Punjabi singer-actor who has become one of India's most prominent global crossover stars, brushed off questions about his US citizenship status with characteristic wit, quipping about a Green Card and declining to say anything definitive: 'I'm not saying anything.'

The question has gained currency given Diljit's increasingly international lifestyle. He has spent considerable time in the United States in recent years, performing sold-out concert tours that have taken him to arenas across North America and establishing a profile that rivals his Bollywood peers in terms of cultural reach, if not box-office dominance.

For his enormous fanbase in India and across the Punjabi diaspora, Diljit represents something more than entertainment — he is seen as a cultural touchstone, someone who has carried the spirit of Punjab to global stages while maintaining his roots in the language, music and sensibility of home. The citizenship question, therefore, is not merely biographical curiosity but touches on identity and belonging in a way that few other celebrity questions do.

Diljit's evasive but humorous response is consistent with his public persona — self-aware, never fully revealing, and always leaving his audience wanting more. Whether the Green Card joke was a genuine hint or simply a deflection, it has generated exactly the kind of conversation the star seems content to let run.
key_facts: Diljit Dosanjh declined to confirm or deny seeking US citizenship
Made a Green Card joke when asked directly
His global profile has grown sharply through international concert tours

stories.headline: Is King's Budget Really Rs 450 Crore? Director Addresses the Buzz Around Shah Rukh–Suhana Film
stories.what: Speculation is swirling that King, the upcoming film starring Shah Rukh Khan and his daughter Suhana Khan, carries a budget of Rs 450 crore — a figure that would make it one of the most expensive Bollywood productions ever. The film's director has now responded to these reports, though the exact nature of the response — confirmation or denial — leaves room for continued debate. King marks Suhana Khan's mainstream Bollywood debut alongside her father, making it one of the most anticipated Hindi films in the pipeline.
stories.lens: At Rs 450 crore, King would be among Bollywood's costliest films ever — the scale of the investment matters because it sets the bar for what the industry considers a viable blockbuster, and ultimately it's ticket prices and multiplex economics that audiences feel directly.
stories.article:
The budget of King, the highly anticipated film pairing Shah Rukh Khan with daughter Suhana Khan, has become the subject of intense industry speculation, with reports suggesting a figure of Rs 450 crore. The film's director has now weighed in on the claims, adding a new layer to what is already one of Bollywood's most-watched productions.

King is significant for multiple reasons: it represents Suhana Khan's mainstream Hindi film debut, a moment the Khan family's enormous fanbase has long awaited. Shah Rukh Khan, whose recent films have demonstrated his undiminished box-office pull, is reportedly playing a complex lead role alongside her, with the father-daughter dynamic at the film's emotional core.

If the Rs 450 crore figure is accurate, King would rank among the most expensive Bollywood productions ever mounted, surpassing the budgets of several recent pan-India blockbusters. Such a scale would also imply extraordinary pressure on the film to perform at the box office, both domestically and internationally, to recoup its investment.

The director's public response to the budget reports — whether a clarification or a deflection — signals that the production team is aware of the scrutiny the project is under. With no release date yet confirmed, every piece of information about King is being parsed closely by trade analysts and fans alike.
key_facts: King reportedly budgeted at Rs 450 crore
Film stars Shah Rukh Khan and Suhana Khan
Director has responded to the budget reports
Marks Suhana Khan's mainstream Bollywood debut
